definition: The Transcription Factor IID (TFIID) complex is a multimeric protein complex composed of TATA-binding protein (TBP) and TBP-associated factors (TAFs), including TAF4, that plays a central role in transcription initiation; pathogenic variants in its subunit genes disrupt brain development and give rise to neurodevelopmental disorders termed TAF-opathies.

source.title: De novo putative loss‐of‐function variants in TAF4 are associated with a neuro‐developmental disorder
source.quote: TATA-binding protein associated factor 4 (TAF4) is a subunit of the Transcription Factor IID (TFIID) complex, a central player in transcription initiation. Other members of this multimeric complex have been implicated previously as monogenic disease genes in human developmental disorders.
